title: Induced interoceptive imprecision should lower presence

statements.text: Artificially making interoceptive predictions imprecise should diminish conscious presence and alter anterior insula activity, while simply raising interoceptive prediction error should increase anxiety instead.
statements.falsification_criteria: Interoceptive predictions made imprecise without any drop in presence, or raised interoceptive prediction error without any rise in anxiety.

prediction.resolution_criterion: An experiment that makes interoceptive predictions imprecise reports lower presence and abnormal anterior insula activity, and one that raises interoceptive prediction error reports more anxiety.

sources.quote: artificially induced imprecision in interoceptive predictions should lead to diminished conscious presence and abnormal AIC activity; by contrast, simple elevation of interoceptive prediction error signals should lead instead to increased anxiety.
